clues: This city sits in the far north of Alaska where two big rivers meet. It is far south of the Arctic Circle but still deep in the wild north.
In winter, cold air pools in this valley city while warm air rises to the hills. It has one of the biggest such flips on Earth.
A man set up a trade post by the river in 1901. Gold was found close by soon after, and crowds of miners rushed in.
After oil was found far to the north, this city sent food and tools to the crews. It helped build the great pipe that moves oil south.
The main state school here was the first one in its whole state school group. It first opened its doors back in nineteen seventeen.
